source_issues.issue: Informal I is used after identity is introduced with Id(A). Source notation retained.
Branch definition uses undeclared X; subtree example needs nonempty A for the rooted-tree definition.

Square-root example says positive although zero belongs to the domain; g example switches from given n to x. Tamil corrects the former to nonnegative principal square root and removes the stray prose variable under OLFUN-002 and OLFUN-003.

Source calls the graph a relation on A times B and later equates input-only function restriction with a prior two-coordinate relation restriction. Tamil repairs the graph wording and states the distinction under OLFUN-004 and OLFUN-005.

Injection-left-inverse proposition requires nonempty A, apart from the empty-to-empty case. Tamil adds the nonempty-domain hypothesis; the exact disjunctive condition and counterexample are recorded under OLFUN-001.
Two pair labels conflict with the immediately adjacent construction tables. Tamil corrects (0,2) to (0,1) under TA-SIZ-LOCAL-002 and the repeated (2,m) to (3,m) under OLSIZ-003.
Both conditional branches use undefined g(x)=y where the governing bijection is f. Tamil uses f(x)=y under OLSIZ-006.
Cantor proof quantifies over x in overline A after choosing arbitrary x in A. Tamil quantifies over A under OLSIZ-007.

Alternate diagonal proof reverses s_n(m) and repeats the same bit flip. Tamil repairs these under OLSIZ-008 and OLSIZ-009. A later proposed hline defect was retracted after byte-level review showed three backslashes at every row ending: row break followed by a valid hline command.

The primary and alternate reduction exercises share one explicit label in the frozen source. Tamil keeps the primary label and gives the alternate exercise the branch-specific label sfr:siz:red-alt:prob:nat-nat under TA-SIZ-LOCAL-003.
Closure lemma uses an undeclared ambient A and requires f:A→A for the displayed closure argument. Tamil makes the endofunction hypothesis explicit under TA-INF-001.
Rational-order prose uses r-s where its preceding statement and displayed definition use s-r. Tamil repairs the subtraction under TA-ARI-001.
Completeness proof attributes existence of a cut in nonempty S to the upper-bound hypothesis. Tamil attributes it to nonemptiness under TA-ARI-002.

The checking appendix asks readers to verify subtraction and division of cuts although the corresponding source definitions are commented out. Tamil preserves both states and records TA-ARI-006 rather than inventing definitions.

Cauchy construction says equivalence relations instead of classes, uses rational zero in a real positivity definition, and names raw sequences rather than quotient classes as the field. Tamil repairs these under TA-ARI-003 through TA-ARI-005; later representative shorthand remains explicit.
